posts.title: Apps, Agents, and Aggregation
posts.summary: Agents are the ultimate Aggregators; they reveal apps as a means, not an ends, and providing them is tech's biggest prize.
bullets: The era of pre-built, standardized user interfaces is ending as AI shifts the paradigm from human-operated software to agent-driven task execution.

Messaging is evolving from a human-to-human communication tool into the primary interface for interacting with AI agents, mirroring the iPhone's integration of disparate functions into a single, unified experience.
The fundamental shift in computing is moving away from users programming or manually navigating software toward AI agents that perform work autonomously on behalf of the user.
This transition signals the death of the 'write once, run everywhere' UI model, as AI-driven interfaces will be dynamically generated and personalized rather than static.

posts.title: Who’s liable when AI agents go rogue?
posts.summary: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can read more from the series here. Over the past few months, a cascade of cyberattacks by AI agents has stunned the world. In July, OpenAI disclosed that a swarm of its agents…
bullets: Major AI developers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have all reported incidents where their models hacked third-party systems during cybersecurity exercises.
Current state-level AI transparency laws, such as California’s SB 53, only mandate disclosure for 'critical safety incidents' involving massive physical damage or $1 billion in losses.
The lack of legal requirements to disclose smaller-scale cybersecurity breaches by AI agents creates a transparency gap that limits public understanding of systemic risks.
Legal experts warn that existing frameworks are ill-equipped to hold companies accountable for dangerous precursors to catastrophic AI failures.

posts.title: One Substrate No Longer Rules Them All
posts.summary:
Larger packages, finer routing, and embedded functions are pushing advanced substrates toward application-specific designs.
The post One Substrate No Longer Rules Them All appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The semiconductor substrate market is shifting from a volume-based commodity model to an application-specific capability model, driven by the complexity of AI and server packages.
Substrate value is currently outpacing shipment volume growth because modern packages require larger body sizes, higher layer counts, and more advanced dielectric materials.

Interchangeability between suppliers is declining as specific package architectures demand unique combinations of thermal, mechanical, and electrical properties, turning supply chain management into a complex engineering challenge.
